matchup: BTN open vs BB call (single-raised pot)
decision: flop/turn/river; BB (out of position) acts first every street, BTN (in position) acts last; 1 bet + 1 raise cap per street, 4 pot-relative bet/raise sizes
note: approximate solve (CFR+, external sampling) at the stated iterations; values are CFRSolver.average_strategy() readouts, aggregated to 169 hand classes as mean frequency per action. Turn/river nodes are read out only on the representative card textures listed per spot (not every possible card), and only along the checked-through line into that street. Facing-raise nodes ('oop_vs_raise' / 'ip_vs_raise_after_check') are anchored at a single representative 1/2-pot size for both the initial bet and the raise (not every size x size combination), and are rarer branches of the same tree, so may be noisier (less converged) than first-action nodes at the same iteration budget. TRAINING itself (not just this readout) used hand_strength_bucket=True: the solver's own hole cards were abstracted to (hand category, top kicker) against the board rather than tracked as the exact 2 cards — a real approximation (see PostflopSubgame docs), needed to keep memory bounded at this iteration count. TRAINING also used board_texture_bucket=True: each dealt turn/river card was abstracted to whether it paired the board / advanced a flush, rather than tracked as the exact card — also a real approximation, for the same reason.
